entities.name: Karomama Meritmut
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Karomama Meritmut (prenomen: Sitamun Mutemhat) was an ancient Libyan high priestess and a God's Wife of Amun during Egypt's Twenty-Second Dynasty, specifically during the reign of Pharaoh Sheshonq I (c. 945–924 BCE).

Born into the Ma tribe, a powerful and ancient Libyan people, Karomama Meritmut's significance lies in her role as a mediator between the Egyptian and Libyan cultures, as well as her influence on the development of the Twenty-Second Dynasty.

Karomama Meritmut was part of a complex network of priestesses and high-ranking officials who played crucial roles in the governance and spirituality of the dynasty.

Her legacy extends to the preservation of Libyan cultural heritage and the blending of Libyan and Egyptian traditions, which would later shape the trajectory of ancient Egyptian history.

As a testament to her importance, Karomama Meritmut's name has been inscribed on several artifacts found in Thebes, including a granite statue discovered at the site of the Temple of Amun.
